title: Virtual DC Test Bench and Arduino Uno firmware worker
highlights: A new client-side DC solver adds modeled voltmeter and component-current measurements to the existing interactive Uno circuit builder; floating nodes and unsupported components are explicitly labelled.
The wiring diagram supports selecting a probe with touch or keyboard while keeping breadboard, perspective, schematic, JSON export and static safety checks synchronized.

Successful Arduino Uno .hex artifacts can run in a bounded AVR8js web worker to inspect D2–D13 signals, basic serial output and D13 transitions; no additional Sandbox compile or build credit is required.
ESP32, sensors, power budgets, full SPICE and physical hardware behavior are not emulated. The new validation tests run in the low-cost Vercel prebuild gate.

title: Image model compatibility and automatic wiring fallback
highlights: AI illustrations use a model listed as eligible for free AI Gateway credits through its supported image-generation API.
Accounts intentionally configured for Gemini image models retain the chat image API.
Provider outages or unavailable AI allowance show the free illustrated wiring view; invalid or electrically rejected connections remain blocked.
One credit is charged only for a usable AI image. The automatic SVG fallback uses no AI credits.

title: Connection endpoint validation and sensor supply checks
highlights: Reject controller self-connections, module labels used as board pins and code aliases without physical terminal names.
Detect incorrect ACS712 3.3 V supply labels in reversed connection rows as well as normal wiring rows.
AI drafts and image requests share connection checks; rejected diagrams reserve no member credits.
Image denials distinguish free-tier model restrictions from generic account or region failures.

title: Module previews and cellular wiring checks
highlights: SIM900A and other recognized module terminals share one device card, with every original pin connection preserved.
UART peripherals remain explicitly unmodeled; concept controls no longer assign HIGH/LOW states to GSM terminals.
Unverified cellular modem power and direct 5 V UART RX wiring block approval; electrical draft failures and image-service failures do not consume member credits.
Image-service failures now report access, authentication, budget or rate-limit categories without exposing provider details.

title: Dedicated paginated component catalog
highlights: The component catalog now has its own /catalog page, linked from the home page and Studio product links.
Search, category, sort, page size and pagination share URL state, with 12, 24 or 48 products per page.
More visible Bootstrap cards, grid, filters, breadcrumbs, buttons and pagination, with the existing cart and checkout flow retained.

title: Bootstrap styling foundation
highlights: Locally hosted Bootstrap 5.3.8 styles are shared across CircuitByte application pages, storefront and order tracking.
Studio uses Bootstrap form, navigation and button classes while retaining its branding and gated workflow.
Existing React/native interactions remain in control; no extra JavaScript framework or runtime CDN is required.

title: Guided build tabs with progression checks
highlights: Idea, Materials, Board, Diagram, Code, Compile and Upload are now sequential tabs. Each step explains its requirements and locks later steps until they are met.
Materials and board suggestions follow the idea. Users can list their own exact materials when suggestions do not fit; custom details are included in AI requests and browser/JSON drafts.

Earlier changes invalidate later confirmations. Upload requires a matching successful Studio compile or explicit self-reported Arduino IDE verification. Hardware reviews remain user-confirmed, not certifications.

title: A clearer guided build and better wiring diagrams
highlights: Select, analyze and build steps now show the next actions and component-specific questions, with Arduino IDE download guidance.
Code aliases are no longer drawn as physical modules; invalid alias destinations are excluded with a regeneration notice. Repeated same-direction connections are deduplicated.
Compact board proportions, grouped module cards, richer ACS712/LED artwork and a gridded wiring canvas. Detailed and optional AI views are collapsed.
ACS712 3.3 V supply plans are flagged, with ADC protection and voltage-measurement guidance for power-meter projects.

title: Interactive project preview and clearer electrical findings
highlights: Live Preview now includes an assembled hardware scene with signal playback and a separate interactive concept demo for sample sensor inputs, thresholds, display text and servo angle.
Board-prefixed power and ground labels are normalized; duplicate electrical findings are removed. Unknown findings now read Needs verification.
Concept controls do not execute or change firmware. Missing ratings and board-specific pin constraints still require verification.

title: Illustrated hardware connection view
highlights: Automatic board-and-module illustrations with colored wires from the project connection plan.
Zoom, connection highlighting, full terminal labels and downloadable SVG. No image-generation request is needed for this view.
Illustrations use symbolic terminal positions; follow actual hardware labels. Stale plans remain clearly marked.

title: Library guidance for every store product
highlights: Library coverage now follows all 101 current store products, with recommendations beside selected materials and a searchable product coverage list.
Added product mappings for ACS712, DS1302 and rotary encoders, plus optional ultrasonic, gas sensor, switch, modem, OLED and motor-control libraries.
AI drafts receive product-specific library guidance. Generic sensor models require identification; passive parts and basic GPIO modules are marked as needing no dedicated library.

title: Arduino Library Manager catalog in Studio
highlights: LiquidCrystal_I2C.h and ACS712.h now have direct library mappings. LCD sketches using LiquidCrystal I2C no longer install hd44780 solely because an LCD was selected.
Search the official Arduino Library Manager catalog by name, author or header, and select packages for your build. Dependencies install on demand.

Unknown headers are checked against catalog metadata; ambiguous matches request a library choice. Core and ZIP headers are left for Arduino CLI to resolve. Board compatibility and library APIs still require review.

title: A cleaner project workspace
highlights: Board, materials and project description now form three clear setup steps beside the workbench.
Examples, saved drafts and account settings are grouped in expandable sections. Release notes, USB tools and the project coach remain available without crowding the editor.
Compact page header, a wider desktop editor and a single-column phone/tablet layout. Failed electrical checks and compiler feedback remain visible.

title: GitHub Copilot connection prepared
highlights: Optional GitHub connection and Copilot provider selection for AI drafts and compiler repairs are implemented. Administrator OAuth and runtime setup is required before activation.
Each connected user uses their own Copilot subscription. Existing Studio request limits and electrical review still apply.
Copilot requests do not silently fall back to another paid provider. Image illustrations remain a separate AI Gateway service.

title: Automatic AI wiring illustrations
highlights: Illustrations start automatically in the background when a signed-in user has a project connection plan and AI access. No Generate button is needed.
Tab changes reuse the same attempt and image in the current workspace. Failed attempts do not automatically retry.
Edited sketches can still show an illustration of their existing wiring plan, with a clear reminder to check GPIO assignments.
One shared AI credit is used per new plan; download the image to retain it after a page reload.

title: AI wiring illustrations, ESP/Nano flashing and responsive Studio
highlights: Generate an illustrated board-and-module wiring guide on demand, with colored wires, pin mapping and voltage notes. One shared AI credit per request; compare the image against the exact connection table.
The free connection guide has a cleaner board view, readable pin cards, zoom and SVG download.
Browser flashing now includes classic Nano (new/old bootloaders), ESP8266, ESP32, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3 and M5Stack Core, with chip checks and transfer verification. Hardware UAT is pending.
The support table distinguishes code/compile, diagram and upload capabilities. Mega and Leonardo still use Arduino IDE for upload.
Phone and tablet layouts use touch-sized controls, scrollable tabs and readable wiring details. Desktop Chrome/Edge is recommended for USB work.
This release is handed to the owner for UAT without automated test-suite or browser-test runs.

title: Connected board diagrams and shoppable parts
highlights: Every listed board now has a connection map generated from its project wiring rows.
Simple numeric GPIO HIGH/LOW sequences can be previewed across all board targets; unsupported firmware is explicitly labelled.
Connections highlight supported digital output states; edited sketches pause the wiring overlay until regenerated.
Parts / BOM reads current Product List prices and available stock, with individual Buy buttons and a required-parts cart action.
Unlisted boards, out-of-stock products, optional parts and missing supplies remain visible; checkout verifies prices and availability.

title: Project Success Coach and AI compiler repair
highlights: Adaptive guidance now identifies missing parts, vague requirements, unverified GPIO ratings, electrical warnings, and next steps.
A failed compilation can trigger an explicit quota-counted AI repair without deleting the old browser draft.
Potential secrets in code or diagnostics are rejected before AI repair.
Users can record physical bench checks; software results do not guarantee hardware function.

title: Common modules, release notices & reviewed knowledge
highlights: 30 curated module profiles cover GSM, GPS, RFID, wireless, displays, actuators and common sensors.
Every module has What's This explanations, beginner How To steps, recommended libraries and a first experiment.
One-click example prompts and catalog-linked tutorials guide students through their selected modules.
Reviewed Studio knowledge, opt-in member submissions and vetted external-source research are available.
Release notices show the deployed Git commit so users can identify the exact build under UAT.

title: Multi-board Studio and serial module starters
highlights: Expanded selectable Arduino/ESP board targets to 10 profiles.
Added educational SIM900A GSM, NEO-6M GPS and HC-05 serial starter sketches.
Board-specific library selection, saved wiring recovery and conservative electrical warnings improved.

title: Community affiliation review improvements
highlights: Improved administrator approval and revocation of school listings while respecting public consent.

title: AI netlists and electrical-review safeguards
highlights: AI drafts now include structured netlists when available.
Warnings identify incomplete pin assignments, power references and unverified component ratings.
